# HUD NSPIRE Property Inspection Compliance Kit

> Official regulatory self-audit, scoring simulation, and administrative preparation system for Section 8, Housing Choice Voucher (HCV), and HUD-assisted multifamily property owners and operators. Built under Title 24 of the Code of Federal Regulations (24 CFR Part 5 Subpart G).

## Overview
The National Standards for the Physical Inspection of Real Estate (NSPIRE) replaced the legacy UPCS/HQS standards for all HUD programs, including Public Housing, Section 8 Multifamily Housing, Housing Choice Vouchers (HCV), and CPD programs. NSPIRE shifts inspection emphasis directly to resident health and safety inside the living unit.

Under NSPIRE, defects are categorized into three affirmative severity tiers:
1. **Life-Threatening (LT)**: Mandatory 24-hour repair and photo-proof verification window. Failure results in immediate suspension or abatement of Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) voucher subsidies.
2. **Severe**: Mandatory 24-hour or 30-day repair window depending on program classification.
3. **Moderate / Low**: 30-day or 60-day corrective windows with points deducted from the property's composite 100-point REAC score.

## Primary Inspection Focus Areas
- **The Living Unit (50%+ Scoring Weight)**: Evaluates resident units for life-safety compliance, including sealed smoke alarms, CO detectors, GFCI electrical receptacles within 6 feet of water sources, operational egress windows, hot water temperature (100°F - 120°F), and gas leak prevention.
- **Inside Areas**: Common corridors, basements, laundry facilities, mechanical rooms, electrical service rooms, and fire suppression risers.
- **Outside Areas**: Building envelopes, roofs, gutters, exterior stairs, handrails, parking surfaces, and municipal site grading.

## Top 10 Immediate Life-Threatening (24-Hour) Failure Items
1. **Smoke Alarms**: Missing, dead batteries, or non-sealed batteries in battery-only alarms. Requires alarms in every bedroom, immediate hallway, and each level.
2. **Carbon Monoxide (CO) Alarms**: Missing CO alarms on any level with fuel-burning appliances or attached garages.
3. **GFCI Receptacles**: Missing or malfunctioning Ground Fault Circuit Interrupters within 6 feet of any sink or water source.
4. **Water Heater Temperature & Pressure Relief (TPR) Valve**: Missing, plugged, or incorrectly pitched discharge pipe terminating more than 6 inches above the floor.
5. **Bedroom Window Egress**: Windows nailed shut, painted shut, or blocked by heavy AC units preventing emergency fire escape.
6. **Double-Cylinder Deadbolt Locks**: Locks requiring an interior key to exit the property (severe entrapment hazard).
7. **Electrical Panel Hazards**: Missing breaker blanks or unsealed knockout holes allowing accidental contact with live busbars.
8. **Exposed Electrical Wiring**: Missing outlet or switch plate covers; uncapped open splice wires.
9. **Natural Gas / Propane Leaks**: Detectable raw gas odor or unvented fuel-fired heaters in sleeping quarters.
10. **Structural Fall Hazards**: Missing or loose guardrails/handrails on porches, decks, or stairwells with 4+ risers or over 30 inches above grade.

## Compliance Tooling & Deliverables
- **Top 25 Immediate Failures Guide**: Plain-English, 24-hour priority punchlist with 5-minute contractor fixes.
- **Master Room-by-Room 67-Standard Checklist**: Clipboard-ready audit sheet covering units, common spaces, and grounds.
- **Tenant Preparation Notice & 48-Hour Inspection Letter**: Ready-to-send tenant notice letter explaining access and unit prep requirements.
- **Handyman Scope of Work (SOW)**: Pre-formatted work order template for maintenance contractors.
- **45-Day Technical Review & Dispute Rebuttal Kit**: Formal administrative appeal letters for contesting improper REAC deductions.
- **HUD Scoring Simulation Model**: Multi-unit scoring algorithm reflecting current HUD Federal Register notices (Docket No. FR-6086-N-04 / 2026-19881).
- **Federal Register Regulatory Radar**: Automated compliance daemon monitoring HUD notices and standards amendments.

## Canonical Statutory References
- Standard: 24 CFR Part 5 Subpart G (Physical Condition Standards and Inspection Requirements)
- Rule: 88 FR 30442 (Economic Growth Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act: Implementation of NSPIRE)
- Scoring Notice: 88 FR 43382 / Docket No. FR-6086-N-04
- Official Portal: https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/public_and_indian_housing/reac/nspire
